chunks: From him, from Abu Ishaq, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).

Regarding two men who had two dirhams between them, one said, 'The two dirhams are mine,' and the other said, 'They are between me and you.' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'He has acknowledged that one of the two dirhams is not his at all, and that it belongs to his partner, but as for the other, it is between them.'

key_terms.لَيْسَ لَهُ فِيهِ شَيْءٌ: He has no share in it

ai.seo_question: How is a dispute over jointly held money resolved when one party claims full ownership?
ai.summary: In this ruling from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) applies the principle of *qarar* (confirmation) to resolve a financial dispute, establishing that a claimant's admission of partial ownership for the opponent validates that share. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the weight of self-incriminating testimony in civil cases, ensuring equitable distribution based on explicit acknowledgment rather than mere presumption. The case illustrates the practical application of evidentiary standards in early Islamic legal theory, where partial admission serves as conclusive proof for the admitted portion.
